messages:
maya.ops: Heads up — we're bringing up eu-west-3 GPU cluster (8x A100, Dedicated pool) next Tue. Need a crisp security baseline + handoff checklist before the infra runbook is published. Can eng-infra + security review?

maya.ops: Goals: IAM role design, secrets handling, KMS/HSM integration for disk + service secrets, automated policy checks in CI, and a clear owner for post-handoff support.

liam.sec: @maya.ops +1. Proposed minimal IAM roles: cluster-controller-role (assumed via OIDC, kube-system SA), node-role (least privileges), kms-encryptor-role (only Encrypt/Decrypt for specific CMKs). Keep permissions narrow — no wildcard actions. Example trust policy (aws EKS OIDC):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"Federated": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.example"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
    "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"oidc.eks.example:sub": "system:serviceaccount:kube-system:node-controller"}}
  }]
}
```
Add an enforced rotation schedule for any long-lived credentials and prefer short-lived tokens (IRSA).

devon.inf: On secrets: recommend Vault with KMS auto-unseal for hosted, and HSM-backed KMS for Private deployments. If Vault isn't available, use envelope encryption with regional CMKs and store ciphertext in Secrets Manager/Parameter Store. Ensure CSI driver uses SecretProviderClass with read-only mounts. Example Vault auto-unseal note:
```bash
vault operator init -recovery-shares=1 -recovery-threshold=1
# then configure auto-unseal with KMS/HSM provider
```
Also: no embedded credentials in AMI bake pipelines.

olivia.sre: Policy gating: run Conftest/OPA rules against terraform plan and kube manifests. CI job `infra-validate` should run `conftest test ./tfplan.json` and fail on policy violations. Checklists: KMS CMK presence, EBS encryption enabled, no public SGs, OIDC provider exists.

deploy-bot: [automation] Created INFRA-523: "eu-west-3 security baseline + handoff" and assigned to @maya.ops — https://links.example/INFRA-523

maya.ops: Infra specifics to note: node pools will be tainted `gpu:dedicated=true` and use a dedicated node-role. Node IAM must only allow Describe/Attach for EBS and kms:Encrypt/Decrypt on the CMK alias `alias/redwood-euw3`. Kubelet should have `--rotate-certificates` enabled. NVMe/disk encryption must be enforced at instance launch.

liam.sec: Runtime integrity: require encrypted root and ephemeral volumes, and prefer attestation (Nitro-based attestation on AWS) for Dedicated customers. For HSM integration use CloudHSM or KMS custom key store; store CMK ARNs in our secret metadata so automation can look them up.

devon.inf: Validation scripts I'd like to add to the runbook: `scripts/check-security-baseline.sh` that verifies: CMK exists, iam role trust configured, kms:Decrypt allowed for autoscaler SA, EBS encryption flag true, OIDC provider present, no wildcard IAM policies. Quick checks: 
```bash
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/redwood-euw3
kubectl get sa -n kube-system autoscaler -o yaml | grep -E 'eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn'
```
Failures should block promotion to prod.

caroline.pmo: For the handoff — what are concrete acceptance criteria? We need items we can tick off in the ticket for sign-off.

maya.ops: Proposed acceptance criteria: 1) Terraform apply succeeded in staging with plan audited; 2) Conftest/OPA tests passed; 3) Security validation script returns green; 4) 24h smoke run (health + canary jobs) with SLOs met; 5) sign-off from infra owner (maya.ops) + security (liam.sec). After that we hand to SRE oncall for 48h monitoring.

olivia.sre: Add alerting requirements before handoff: KMS key rotation failures, kubelet cert expiration warnings, node pool unhealthy >5% for 10m, and unexpected IAM policy changes. These alerts must be in the runbook with playbook links.

maya.ops: I'll update the runbook with these checks and add the validation scripts to the repo. Will ping the group tomorrow for a quick sign-off call. Thanks all :pray:
